title: Earth Built a Nuclear Reactor 2 Billion Years Ago

vo.text: Two billion years ago, Earth built its own working nuclear reactor.
vo.imagePrompt: Ancient glowing subterranean uranium deposit deep underground, cyan radiation energy pulsing through wet stone, hyperrealistic cinematic lighting, vertical 9:16

vo.text: In Oklo, Gabon, underground water met highly enriched natural uranium ores.
vo.imagePrompt: Cross section of ancient African cave bedrock with groundwater seeping into glowing uranium veins, dramatic shadows, vertical composition

vo.text: Water slowed down neutrons, triggering a sustained nuclear chain reaction.
vo.imagePrompt: Subatomic particle simulation, blue Cherenkov radiation light wave pulsating through liquid water molecules, dark space background

vo.text: Pause—how did this natural power plant avoid blowing itself apart?
vo.imagePrompt: Deep underground rocky chamber overheating, steam bubbling up through fractured stone, red danger glow, dramatic wide angle vertical

vo.text: It built a self-regulating safety system without human control.
vo.imagePrompt: Thermal steam vents opening in ancient rock, blue energy calming down to steady pulse, golden hour glow underground, ultra detailed

vo.text: Heat boiled away water, stopping fission until it cooled.
vo.imagePrompt: Water vapor evaporating from glowing blue mineral crystal, cycles of light dimming and rising, macro photography style

vo.text: This alien engine ran for one hundred thousand years.
vo.imagePrompt: Time-lapse effect of underground cavern over millennia, steady blue power grid pattern inside bedrock, cinematic cosmic atmosphere

vo.text: Modern scientists still cannot match its perfect nuclear waste containment.
vo.imagePrompt: Futuristic glass capsule containing glowing ancient rock in clean laboratory setting, contrast of dark room and cyan light
